metadata.title: THE ROLE OF SUBNATIONAL GOVERNMENTS IN ADULT SKILLS SYSTEMS: SLOVENIA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is a governance and institutional mapping of Slovenia’s adult skills system, not an analysis of student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC). As such, there is no sampling frame for students, no complex survey design, and no application of student-level sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife). The tables describe responsibilities and expenditure shares across national and local government levels, so weighting is not relevant to estimation of achievement or PV-based outcomes. For this type of report, the appropriate “data preparation” is compilation of governance information from referenced sources rather than statistical weighting of respondents.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are generated for cognitive achievement scales in ILSA assessments (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC literacy/numeracy), but this document does not analyze any student assessment outcomes. Instead, it summarizes governance structures, stakeholder responsibilities, and expenditure/execution roles across levels of government. Because there is no PV-based dependent variable and no student-level dataset used for estimation, PV handling and missing-data handling are not applicable in the usual ILSA sense.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level or assessment microdata sample is used. The note compiles governance and institutional information for Slovenia from referenced sources and presents it in descriptive tables (e.g., governance model, allocation of responsibilities, and stakeholder roles).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note provides a descriptive overview of how Slovenia’s adult skills system is governed across national and local levels. It characterizes the system as centrally governed, with most design and management at the national level and implementation carried out by national agencies through local branches and municipalities. The note details which policy areas are handled at the national level (e.g., VET/HVET strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, and delivery; CET; AE via municipalities; and ALMPs via the Ministry of Labour and the Employment Service) versus the local level (notably municipalities’ role in implementing AE and funding local providers, and local branches delivering ALMPs). It also reports the share of general government expenditure at the sub-national level (17.5%) and outlines key institutions and their responsibilities. No student assessment data, scaling, or PV-based benchmarks are analyzed, so there are no ML performance metrics or achievement effects to interpret.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a governance/institutional country note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis. Consequently, there is no ILSA microdata sample, no PV-based outcome, and no statistical modeling (including ML) whose results could be extracted. The absence of sample sizes, countries-by-sample breakdowns, and ML metrics reflects the document’s descriptive compilation purpose.
